claims.text: A thin, conformal boron nitride coating on conventional metallic components will mitigate molten-aluminum-induced corrosion.
A thin, conformal boron nitride coating will mitigate mechanical erosion in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Applying a boron nitride coating will extend the service life of hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Conventional steel or alloy rollers and guide plates degrade rapidly when exposed to molten aluminum.
A protective boron nitride coating can be deposited by chemical vapor deposition.
The proposed coating is intended to operate during long-term exposure to molten aluminum at temperatures around or above 660°C.
A conformal boron nitride surface layer can form a barrier between the metallic substrate and molten aluminum.
Boron nitride has sufficient high-temperature stability for the proposed molten-aluminum environment.
Boron nitride is chemically inert with respect to molten aluminum under the proposed conditions.
Boron nitride is non-wetting with respect to molten aluminum.
Preventing direct contact between the substrate metal and molten aluminum reduces corrosion reactions.
Preventing direct contact between the substrate metal and molten aluminum reduces mechanical erosion of the substrate.
Boron-nitride-coated components will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than uncoated components.
Boron-nitride-coated components will undergo less mechanical degradation than uncoated components.
The coating's protective performance depends on its thickness, uniformity, and adhesion under thermal and mechanical stress.
Impurities in molten aluminum may influence the long-term durability of the boron nitride coating.
